samples.summary: Four of the six durability lapse reasons are never asserted as *produced* — only as consumed
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` computes `lapse` as `lost ? 'dropped' : persistDisabled ? 'too-large' : outOfSpace ? 'out-of-space' : writesFailing ? 'write-failed' : unreportable ? 'unreportable' : undefined` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:215-228). `useDurabilityLapse`/`DurabilityLapseScope` appear in only two test files (grep for `useDurabilityLapse|DurabilityLapseScope` over packages/frontend): `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx`, which *injects* each lapse value by hand into a `DurabilityLapseScope` and then asserts `tooltipFor`'s wording, and `src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`, which covers `not-enabled`, `not-permitted`, `another-tab`, `none` and — via a `local-changes-dropped` event — `dropped`. `src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` renders only a `useDocumentDurability()` probe (`function Probe() { return {useDocumentDurability() ? 'durable' : 'not-durable'}; }`), never `useDurabilityLapse()`, so its `persist-disabled`, `onWriteFailure(new Error('refused'))` and subscribe-refused cases assert the boolean and nothing about the reason. In particular the quota branch (`err instanceof DOMException && err.name === 'QuotaExceededError'` → `setOutOfSpace(true)`, line 161-171) is exercised by no test at all — every write-failure case passes a plain `Error`. The design requirement these values exist for is that the tooltip names which case applies; swapping or dropping any of these four arms would show the wrong remedy ("could not be written to" instead of "out of local storage space") with a green suite.
searchedFor: read tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx 'the lapse reaching the chip' describe

samples.summary: Nothing asserts the durable provider forwards rpcAddr/apiKey/metadata/authTokenInjector to the Yorkie client
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` renders `<KeyedYorkieProvider rpcAddr={rpcAddr} apiKey={apiKey} metadata={metadata} authTokenInjector={authTokenInjector} clientKey={clientKey} store={store}>`. The only suite that captures the provider's props is `src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`, and it asserts exactly two of them: `expect(mounted[0].clientKey).toContain(':7:note-7')` and `expect(mounted[0].store).toBeDefined()`. Grepping that file for `authTokenInjector|metadata|rpcAddr` returns no matches. `src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` mocks `YorkieProvider` as `({ children }) => <>{children}</>`, discarding props entirely. A durable client that silently lost `authTokenInjector` would fail to authenticate against the Yorkie auth webhook — a broken editor for every opted-in user — and no test would fail.
searchedFor: grep clientKey assertions across packages/frontend tests

samples.summary: `load()`'s cross-tab `touch()` write is untested — every open-document test is satisfied by the in-memory `touched` set
samples.evidence: `load()` does both `this.touched.add(docKey)` and `void this.touch(docKey)`, and the comment for the latter is explicit that the in-memory set is not enough: "`touched` is this instance's memory, and the ordering eviction reads is shared — so an attach that never writes would stay the oldest row in every *other* tab's view." The test that looks like it covers this — `wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts` "never evicts a document this session has open, even the oldest one" — calls `session.load('opened-but-idle')` and then `session.saveSnapshot(...)` on the *same* instance, so the survival is fully explained by `touched`. No test reopens the database from a second instance after a bare `load` and asserts the `updatedAt` moved. Deleting the `void this.touch(docKey)` line would leave the entire suite green while another tab's sweep could collect a document this tab has open (the lock guard, not the timestamp, is then the only thing left).
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts 'never evicts a document this session has open'
grep touch( and updatedAt assertions in the four wafflebase-doc-store test files

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser`'s skip branch — the cross-account guard on orphan sweeping — has no test
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters with `!known.has(docKey) && !this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)`, where `belongsToAnotherUser` parses `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` out of the store key so the orphan sweep does not delete another account's headerless snapshot. The only orphan test is `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts` "is collected rather than living forever out of reach", which seeds `doc-a` (a key with no `wb:` segment at all, so the regex never matches and the guard always returns `false`). No test seeds an orphan under a key like `pk/wb:abc:user-2:sheet-9/sheet-9` and asserts it survives a `collectStale` run by user-1. The guard's true branch is dead as far as the suite is concerned.
searchedFor: grep 'wb:' key fixtures in the wafflebase-doc-store test files

samples.summary: The `saved-locally` toast's latch and recovery/retraction arm are not covered
samples.evidence: The `savedLocally` branch sets `warned.current = true` and shows `toast.info('Saved to this device', { id: TOAST_ID, description: connected ? ... : ... })`, and the comment says it is latched "so the recovery arm below retracts this one too and confirms once the work actually reaches the server". The only durable-toast test in `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` is "says where the work went instead of saying nothing", which drives the disconnected case and asserts only that `info` was called with a title matching /this device/. Grepping that file for `dismiss` shows the only `expect(dismiss).toHaveBeenCalled()` is at line 348, inside the pre-existing stranded-unmount test. Nothing drives `saved-locally` → reconnect → `saved` and asserts the toast is dismissed and the success receipt shown, and the `connected` (server-rejecting-pushes) description of the info toast is never asserted. A regression that left a stale "Saved to this device" notice on screen after the work reached the server, or that showed the connection-dropped wording to a user whose connection is fine, would pass.
searchedFor: read the 'SyncStatusChip on a durable document' describe in that file

samples.summary: `dropAllForUser`'s `keepArchives` option (and `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser`) have no caller and no test
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` gates `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...)`, and `eraseOfflineData` threads an identical `{ keepArchives?: boolean }` through (offline-erase.ts:30). Grepping `keepArchives` across packages/frontend returns only those two declaration sites and the doc comment — no caller ever passes it (the 401 path in this diff now erases nothing at all rather than erasing with archives kept), and no test in `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` or `offline-erase.test.ts` exercises `keepArchives: true`. Same for `dropArchivesWhere`'s third parameter `onlyUser`, which both call sites omit. If the branch is wrong it cannot be detected; if it is genuinely dead it is untested surface area carrying a promise about not deleting the only copy of unsent work.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts 'drops a user's archives on logout'

samples.summary: An assertion in the identity-change test cannot observe what its comment claims
samples.evidence: The test comments `// And nothing is left mounted under the previous person's key.` and then asserts `expect(mounted.filter((props) => props.clientKey === first)).toHaveLength(1)`. `mounted` is an array pushed to from the `YorkieProvider` mock's render body, so it records renders, never mounts or unmounts — the identity file's own comment says as much ("the mock records a props object per render, so a re-render is expected"). The assertion therefore says "the old key was rendered exactly once", which is not the stated property; a provider genuinely left mounted under the old key that simply did not re-render would satisfy it. The preceding assertions in the test are sound, so the case is not vacuous overall — this one line just does not carry the weight its comment gives it.
searchedFor: read the 're-decides when the person signed in changes underneath it' test
read the YorkieProvider mock in collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx and -identity.test.tsx

samples.summary: The route-param traversal guard was loosened from every-request to some-request
samples.evidence: The loop previously asserted, per URL, both `not.toContain('/auth/logout')` and `toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))`. The diff keeps the first per-URL but replaces the second with a single `expect(paths.some((pathname) => pathname.includes(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)))).toBe(true)`. The stated justification (a companion request such as `deleteWorkspace`'s document listing carries no id) is real, and the `/auth/logout` check still catches an unencoded id in a path. But the property is now weaker: a call that issues two id-bearing requests and encodes only one of them, or that places a raw id somewhere `..` does not normalize into `/auth/logout` (a query string, a fragment), is no longer caught by the second assertion. A per-URL exemption list for requests that legitimately carry no id would keep the original strength.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/src/api/url.test.ts around the traversal describe
read workspaces.ts documentIdsIn to confirm the companion request carries no id

finding.summary: The lapse value CollabDocumentProvider computes (unsupported / not-permitted / not-enabled / another-tab) is never asserted by any test
finding.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx` derives `lapse` from `supportsClientKey()`, `permitted`, `offlineEnabled` and the election, and publishes it via `DurabilityLapseScope`. Every test that exercises lapse behaviour injects the value by hand: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632` and `:865` wrap the chip in `<DurabilityLapseScope lapse={...}>` directly, and `sync-status-tooltip.ts` is tested as a pure function. Grepping `lapse|Lapse` across `src/components/__tests__` returns nothing (only an unrelated loader comment), and the two durable provider suites (`collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`, `collab-document-provider-identity.test.tsx`) assert only `clientKey`/`store`/mount counts. So the mapping from provider state to cause is uncovered: if it collapsed to `not-permitted`, the chip's `offerOffline` (`sync-status-chip.tsx:84`, `lapse !== 'not-permitted'`) would silently disappear on every non-durable document — the design's second entry point for turning the feature on — and no test would fail. (Impact is currently deferred because `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to 0.7.22 so `supportsClientKey()` is false, but the gap ships permanently and goes live on a one-line bump.)

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test asserts the lapse value CollabDocumentProvider computes. A dedicated suite does exactly that: `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:556-638` ("the lapse it publishes") mounts the real `CollabDocumentProvider` with a probe reading the real `useDurabilityLapse()` (import at :112) and asserts every branch of the derivation at `collab-document-provider.tsx:303-310`: 'not-enabled' (:577-580), 'not-permitted' via the real `NonDurableScope` (:582-586), 'another-tab' after a simulated second tab (:588-599), 'none' while durable (:601-606), 'none' on a build without client-key support (:608-618), and the durable client's lapse overruling the call site through the real nested `DurabilityLapseScope`s (:620-633). The suite is not over-mocked for this purpose: `beforeEach` forces `supportsClientKey()` true (:135, without which lapse would always be undefined) and `durable-document-context` is not mocked; only `@yorkie-js/react` and `@tanstack/react-query` are stubbed. The reviewer's cited search ("grep lapse|Lapse in src/components/__tests__ returns nothing") is contradicted by lines 548/556/558 of that very file, which the reviewer also claims to have read. The specific regression it worried about (collapsing to 'not-permitted' on non-durable documents, hiding the chip's offerOffline) would fail the 'not-enabled' and 'another-tab' cases.

finding.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments`'s `dropArchives` option is never exercised against the real implementation, so the archive-purge on lost workspace access is uncovered
finding.evidence: `api/workspaces.ts:136,167` call `purgeOfflineDocuments(doomed, { dropArchives: true })` — the mechanism that removes archived full-document snapshots when a workspace is deleted or the signed-in member is removed. `workspaces.test.ts:15-16` mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale, so its five `expect(mockPurge).toHaveBeenCalledWith([...], { dropArchives: true })` assertions only prove the argument is forwarded to a stub. `offline-erase.test.ts`'s "a document that was deleted" block (lines 667-703) is the only place the real `purgeOfflineDocuments` runs, and every call there omits the option (`purgeOfflineDocuments(["abc"])`, `(["keep"])`, `(["anon"])`); one of them asserts the *opposite* ("keeps the archives", line 680). Grep for `dropArchives` across `packages/frontend/src` returns only the two call sites, the mocked assertions, and the two lines of the implementation. If the `options.dropArchives ? "drop" : "keep"` mapping at offline-erase.ts:405 were wrong, archives of a workspace the user was removed from would stay on disk and `recoverOfflineCopy` would re-materialize that content as a document the user owns — the exact privacy rule the feature states — with every suite green.

verdict.reason: The claim that `dropArchives` is never exercised against the real implementation is false in this working tree. offline-erase.test.ts:746-766 ("takes the archives when the caller lost access rather than deleted it") calls the real purgeOfflineDocuments(["revoked"], { dropArchives: true }) at line 760 and asserts store.listArchives() is [] (762) and the live entry is gone (763-765). A second test at 768-784 calls purgeOfflineDocuments(["doomed"], { dropArchives: true }) (779) and asserts the other document's archive survives (781-783), covering scoping. Neither is over-mocked: the test file imports fake-indexeddb/auto and the real WafflebaseDocStore (lines 1-15) with no vi.mock of the store or of offline-erase; archives are genuinely created via expectLoss + remove (755-757, 772-776), and the sibling test at 731-744 proves that setup yields an archive. The tests are non-vacuous for the exact mapping at issue: inverting `options.dropArchives ? "drop" : "keep"` (offline-erase.ts:420), which drives purgeDocument's `archives === "drop"` branch (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:940-952), would fail the assertion at 762 and also the "keeps the archives" assertion at 743. The reviewer's cited line range (667-703) does not match the file; the deleted-document describe block is at 718-795, so the finding appears to rest on a stale read.

finding.summary: No test renders the real lapse publishers, so which `DurabilityLapse` each one emits — and which scope wins when both are mounted — is uncovered
finding.evidence: `useDurabilityLapse` has exactly two producers: `collab-document-provider.tsx:350` (`unsupported`/`not-permitted`/`not-enabled`/`another-tab`) and `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:238` (`dropped`/`too-large`/`out-of-space`/`write-failed`/`unreportable`). Grepping `DurabilityLapseScope|useDurabilityLapse` across packages/frontend shows the only test usage is `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632,865-869`, which hand-mounts the scopes with literal lapse values. So every "tooltip names which case applies" assertion (lines 783-841) and the `strandedUnderScopes` block (845-880) passes regardless of what the production components compute. Concretely uncovered: (a) the nesting order at collab-document-provider.tsx:350 — the comment there records that this scope was once mounted *inside* `inner`, which silently swallowed every durable-client reason; re-inverting it today fails no test, because the chip test supplies its own correctly-ordered scopes; (b) `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:164-169`, the `QuotaExceededError → setOutOfSpace(true)` branch, whose only observable effect is the `out-of-space` lapse — `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` fires `onWriteFailure(new Error('refused'))` and asserts only `useDocumentDurability()`, never the lapse; (c) that the share-link route actually publishes `not-permitted`, which is what the chip's offer-suppression (`sync-status-chip.tsx:99`) keys on.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise -- that no test renders the real lapse publishers, and that the only test usage of useDurabilityLapse is the hand-mounted scopes in sync-status-chip.test.tsx -- is factually false. packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx imports the real useDurabilityLapse (line 112) and mounts the real CollabDocumentProvider under a Probe that renders the published lapse. Its describe('the lapse it publishes') block (lines 556-638) asserts each value computed by production code: 'not-enabled' with the preference off (577-580); 'not-permitted' via the real NonDurableScope, the same wrapper the share route uses at shared-document.tsx:1181, which covers sub-claim (c) (582-586); 'another-tab' after a real second-tab election (588-599); and 'none' both while durable (601-606) and on a build that cannot carry a client key (608-618). Sub-claim (a), the nesting order, is covered directly by the case 'lets the durable client overrule the call site, from the real providers' (620-633): it mounts the real CollabDocumentProvider, which renders the real DurableYorkieProvider (collab-document-provider.tsx:361-384), fires the SDK's local-changes-dropped event, and asserts the probe reads 'dropped'. Only @yorkie-js/react is mocked; both DurabilityLapseScope publishers (collab-document-provider.tsx:361 and durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:238) are real, so re-inverting the nesting -- the regression recorded in the comment at collab-document-provider.tsx:352-359 -- would let the outer undefined win and fail that assertion. The file actually executes: vite.config.ts:463 includes src/**/*.test.tsx. Only sub-claim (b), the QuotaExceededError to out-of-space branch at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:166-168, lacks an end-to-end lapse assertion, but that is a narrow edge case inside an absence claim whose headline is disproven by this counterexample.
